headline: Riyadh categorically denies WSJ report that Ansar Allah demanded $51 billion + formal recognition to end attacks on Saudi Arabia
dek: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- Krimly, X, Thursday Nov 5, via WSJ + Tribune] 'I categorically deny the claims published by The Wall Street Journal regarding demands made by this militia. All of this is pure fabrication by the writers or their alleged sources.' [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- WSJ, T2, 'people…
sources: Rayed Krimly, Saudi Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy, on X (primary statement); Wall Street Journal (T2) reports both the original demand claim and the denial
fault_line: Extortion or reparations? Was $51 billion a ransom demand from an Iranian-armed militia, or the price of a decade of Saudi airstrikes and blockade?

sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- Krimly, X, Thursday Nov 5, via WSJ + Tribune] 'I categorically deny the claims published by The Wall Street Journal regarding demands made by this militia. All of this is pure fabrication by the writers or their alleged sources.' [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- WSJ, T2, 'people briefed on the discussions', recorded 1600-01 Nov 5] After Ansar Allah attacked Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea and seized territory commanding Bab al-Mandeb, Riyadh reached out to ask what a negotiated halt would take. The answer: $51 billion to cover years of Saudi strikes and a long blockade, plus formal recognition of Ansar Allah as Yemen's rulers; other figures have since been discussed, but the price of an exit is 'in the tens of billions of dollars'. WSJ notes the Ansar Allah are now pressing toward Aden, seat of the internationally recognised government. Krimly also accused the Ansar Allah of attacking commercial shipping in the Red Sea and civilian/economic facilities and rejecting peace efforts.
sections.what_verified: 1 tiered family (WSJ T2) carries both the demand report and the denial itself -- WSJ's own text reports Krimly's X post, so the denial-as-made is confirmed. Tribune (tribune.com.pk, Express Tribune) relays the denial verbatim but has NO declared tier in the registry and cannot count toward corroboration. The truth of the demand is contested: WSJ stands by its sourcing ('people briefed on the discussions'); Riyadh calls it fabrication. No Ansar Allah response located in-window.
sections.what_disputed: WSJ stands by the report: 'people briefed on the discussions' say $51bn was the answer, other figures discussed since, price 'in the tens of billions'; Ansar Allah pressing toward Aden. Krimly's denial does not address the reported approach itself (Riyadh reaching out after the tanker attacks and Bab al-Mandeb seizure), only the demand. No independent confirmation of the $51bn figure from any Ansar Allah channel in-window.
sections.why_matters: Riyadh calls the $51bn Ansar Allah demand 'pure fabrication' -- but the Wall Street Journal stands by its sources. Who is lying about the price of ending the Yemen war?
sections.context: Background: Riyadh categorically denies WSJ report that Ansar Allah demanded $51 billion + formal recognition to end attacks on Saudi Arabia

totw_analysis: Our read: Riyadh calls the $51bn Ansar Allah demand 'pure fabrication' -- but the Wall Street Journal stands by its sources. Who is lying about the price of ending the Yemen war? The fault line our audience is arguing over: Extortion or reparations? Was $51 billion a ransom demand from an Iranian-armed militia, or the price of a decade of Saudi airstrikes and blockade?
